trigger: EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability-reporting mandates activated September 11 2026, compelling software manufacturers worldwide to automate security scanning inside CI/CD pipelines or face fines of up to €15M.

timeline.event: US Executive Order 14028 mandates SBOM and secure software practices for federal vendors, seeding enterprise-scale DevSecOps demand; DevSecOps market is $3.73B
Log4Shell post-mortem accelerates SCA adoption globally; Sonatype reports surge in dependency-scanning tool purchases as open source risk dominates boardroom agendas
OWASP releases first LLM Top 10, formally classifying prompt injection, training-data poisoning, and supply-chain vulnerabilities as first-class application security risks
EU Cyber Resilience Act enters into force; manufacturers must now document SBOMs in CycloneDX/SPDX format and report actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours by September 2026
GitHub unbundles Advanced Security into standalone Secret Protection ($21/mo) and Code Security ($32/mo), opening GHAS to non-Enterprise GitHub Team customers for the first time
EU CRA reporting obligations go live; Commission publishes practical compliance guidance; Socket closes $60M Series C at $1B valuation and Aikido Security hits $1B valuation in same quarter

pestal.impact: US CISA Secure-by-Design initiative and EU CRA together establish automated security scanning as a compliance floor for software sold to government and enterprise buyers across 30+ countries

Supply chain breaches now cost an average $4.91M and take 267 days to contain (IBM 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report), making AI-driven preventive scanning orders of magnitude cheaper than incident response

'Vibe coding' culture — 25% of Y Combinator W2025 startups reported 95%+ AI-generated codebases — is normalising insecure code at unprecedented velocity, creating a new class of security-unaware developer

AI coding assistants generate 10,000+ new security findings per month per repository and 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities than human developers; AI-native SAST tools now apply semantic reasoning to cut false-positive rates below 15%

CI/CD pipeline security scanning adds meaningful compute overhead; AI-powered tools reducing false positives improve efficiency by cutting unnecessary remediation cycles, lowering net energy consumption per vulnerability resolved

EU CRA active-exploitation reporting from September 11 2026 requires 24-hour notification to CSIRT and ENISA; non-compliance risks fines up to €15M or 2.5% of global annual turnover, directly pressuring CI/CD security budgets

jobs.job: Detect hardcoded secrets and credentials before they reach production or public repos
jobs.solution: AI secrets-scanning engines (GitHub Secret Protection, GitGuardian, Aikido) auto-block PR merges containing API keys and tokens; 6.4% of Copilot-assisted repos leak secrets — 40% above the baseline

jobs.job: Find exploitable open source vulnerabilities without drowning developers in irrelevant CVE noise
jobs.solution: Reachability-aware SCA platforms (Snyk, Endor Labs, Socket.dev) map CVEs to actually reachable code paths, surfacing only the 8-12% of findings that are genuinely exploitable in a given application

jobs.job: Generate machine-readable SBOM inventories required by EU CRA and US EO 14028 for every release artifact
jobs.solution: CI/CD-integrated SBOM generators (Anchore, Endor Labs, Veracode SCA) automatically produce CycloneDX or SPDX inventories on every build commit with full transitive-dependency coverage

jobs.job: Reduce developer alert fatigue — teams ignore 60%+ of SAST findings — without sacrificing security coverage
jobs.solution: AI autofix tools (Checkmarx Developer Assist via MCP, Snyk Agent Fix, Veracode Fix, GitHub Copilot Autofix) generate PR-ready remediation patches, cutting mean-time-to-fix from days to hours

jobs.job: Secure the CI/CD pipeline itself against supply chain poisoning via malicious GitHub Actions or compromised build tools
jobs.solution: Pipeline security platforms (Endor Labs, Legit Security, Wiz Code) continuously audit workflow files, runner permissions, and dependency pinning for tampering or anomalous behaviour

canvas.who: Security engineers, AppSec architects, and DevOps platform engineers at enterprises with 200+ developers who face EU CRA, SOC 2, FedRAMP, or ISO 27001 obligations and are shipping AI-assisted code at velocity
canvas.where: Inside GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and Harness pipelines at the PR gate; inside developer IDEs (VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, Windsurf) as real-time linting; and in security dashboards aggregating findings across all repos
canvas.why_now: EU CRA 24-hour vulnerability-reporting mandates went live September 2026; AI coding tools are introducing exploitable vulnerabilities at 10x historical rates; and supply chain attacks now account for 30% of all enterprise breaches — up from 15% just one year ago
canvas.behavior: Developer teams want security surfaced at PR time as auto-fix patches, not as a post-deployment ticket queue; they reward tools that suppress false positives, integrate into existing IDE workflows, and never slow a CI pipeline beyond 2 minutes
canvas.unmet: No platform yet correlates SBOM inventory, runtime reachability, and agentic AI code flows into a single exploitability score; false-positive rates remain 25-40% for most SAST tools despite AI advances; and securing AI agent-written code (not just AI-assisted human code) is an unsolved frontier

takeaways: Prioritise reachability-aware SCA (Endor Labs, Snyk, Socket.dev) over raw CVE-count dashboards — only 8-12% of open source vulnerabilities are exploitable in any given codebase; chasing the rest burns engineering cycles with zero security ROI

Deploy AI autofix tooling (Checkmarx Developer Assist, Snyk Agent Fix, Veracode Fix, GitHub Copilot Autofix) before Q4 2026 to cut mean-time-to-fix from days to hours and prevent developer alert fatigue from eroding AppSec programme effectiveness

Automate SBOM generation on every CI build now — EU CRA mandates machine-readable CycloneDX or SPDX inventories for all digital products sold in the EU, and manually cataloguing AI-assisted codebases with hundreds of transitive dependencies is operationally infeasible at scale

Treat CI/CD pipeline configuration (GitHub Actions workflow files, runner permissions, dependency pinning) as a primary attack surface — supply chain compromises now average $4.91M and 267 days to contain, making pipeline hardening one of the highest-ROI security investments available
